about: Can you find your iPhone when it's off. Factory #41, backlog row 46, slug findableoff. One hard idea: Apple's iPhone User Guide ('Add your iPhone to Find My') says 'On a supported iPhone, turning on the Find My network allows you to locate your iPhone for up to 24 hours after it's turned off, or up to 5 hours when it's in power reserve mode'; Apple 102648 says the Find My network is 'a crowdsourced network of over a billion Apple devices that use Bluetooth technology to detect the location of an accessory or device, and report their approximate location back to the owner'; it only works with the Find My network switch on, so check yours: Settings > your name > Find My > Find My iPhone, both switches on. Sources read 2026-11-24, see BRIEF.md.

lines.text: Turned off? Your iPhone's still findable.
So how do you find an iPhone that's off?
lines.say: So, how do you find an iPhone that's off?

lines.text: Say you lose it, switched off.
No Wi-Fi. No cellular. Looks gone.
lines.say: No Wi-Fi. No cellular. Looks... gone.

lines.text: But Apple says a supported iPhone can still be located.
For up to 24 hours after it's turned off.
lines.say: For up to twenty-four hours... after it's turned off.

lines.text: Over a billion Apple devices help find it.
They spot it by Bluetooth and report back.
lines.say: They spot it, by Bluetooth, and report back.

lines.text: Except that needs a switch called Find My network.
Check yours: Settings, your name, Find My.
lines.say: Check yours. Settings, your name, Find My.

lines.text: Tap Find My iPhone. Turn both switches on.
Were yours on? Yes or no.
